clue.text: Jets parking in the open aboard ship

indicators.note: aboard puts the following pieces on board, between the two letters standing for a ship

parts.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for steamship
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
a secret that is out is in the open

explanation.surface: Someone describes jets left parked in the open air on the deck of a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' places P and OUT inside SS, the steamship abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouts are jets of liquid, as from a whale or a fountain.

clue.text: Greek dish unfinished, starter of olives

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for dish loses its last letter

parts.note: a plate is a dish

indicators.note: starter of means the opening letter of olives

explanation.surface: A Greek dish served incomplete, with an olive starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek' looks like a cuisine but names the philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Athenian philosopher, a famous Greek.

clue.text: Some drunk in destitution is most cruel

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Being a drunk in poverty is the harshest fate of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'is most cruel' as 'which is most cruel', echoing Shakespeare's 'the most unkindest cut of all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unkindest is the superlative of unkind, meaning cruellest.

clue.text: Insect initially sucks croup on horse

indicators.note: initially means taking the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: An insect starts sucking blood from a horse's hindquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'croup' looks like a horse's rump or a cough, but only its first letter counts.
explanation.definitionFit: A scarab is a dung beetle, an insect sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Moved coal into site

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the two words that follow are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: Coal was shifted into a building site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' shuffles COAL and INTO together.
explanation.definitionFit: A location is a place or position, the same sense as a site.

clue.text: Quickly enjoy appreciative audience

parts.note: to like something is to enjoy it
people applauding are clappers, so an appreciative audience is the clappers

explanation.surface: Enjoy a quick, appreciative crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like the clappers' is a British idiom for very fast, from bell clappers swinging furiously.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at great speed, so it substitutes for an adverb of haste.

clue.text: Not worried about a heartless official

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the official's title is removed

parts.note: a referee is a match official

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off concern about an uncaring official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the central E from REFEREE, leaving REFREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone carefree has no anxieties, so is not worried.

clue.text: Kite's wings parting to beat makes us delighted

indicators.note: parting means the kite's letters split the word for beat

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them

indicators.note: wings are the outer edges, so the first and last letters of kite

explanation.surface: A kite's wings separate in a strong beat, which pleases us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parting' sets K and E inside TAN; 'makes us' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be taken with something is to be charmed by it, so delighted.

clue.text: Suggestions from open individuals

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
ones are single individuals

explanation.surface: Suggestions are invited from candid people.
explanation.definitionFit: Overtones are hints or implications beneath the surface, that is, suggestions.

clue.text: Traveller's support worker in Amazon, perhaps

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
an Amazon warehouse employee who boxes goods is a packer; 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.surface: A traveller's backing comes from someone working in the Amazon rainforest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' looks like the rainforest but is the online retailer, whose warehouses employ packers.
explanation.definitionFit: A backpacker is a budget traveller carrying a rucksack.

clue.text: Recognised audio version of novel

indicators.note: an audio version is what is heard, so the word is entered by its sound

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new

explanation.surface: Someone recognised the audiobook of a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' is not a book here but the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: To have known something is to have recognised it; both are past tenses of identifying.

clue.text: Battered cod wasn't wretched

indicators.note: battered means the letters are beaten out of shape and rearranged, with a nod to fried fish

explanation.surface: A fish-shop complaint: the battered cod wasn't any good at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling downcast is feeling low and dejected, which is to be wretched.

clue.text: Restricted eastern vessel if coming west

indicators.note: in an across entry, coming west means the pieces read right to left

parts.note: a tin is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A restricted eastern ship is allowed to sail west only on condition.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across answer, 'coming west' means reading right to left, so the whole string is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finite has limits, so it is restricted rather than endless.

clue.text: Regularly provided help, never pointed weapon

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter across the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone regularly gave help but never carried a pointed weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of HELP NEVER are taken; 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An épée is a fencing sword with a pointed tip, so a pointed weapon.

clue.text: Way bats reproduce

indicators.note: bats, as in batty or crazy, means the letters go haywire

explanation.surface: A natural-history fact: this is how bats breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying mammals but is the anagram signal, meaning crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A procedure is a method or way of doing something.

clue.text: Electronic help to resolve: insect that might be African

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

indicators.note: to resolve the letters is to work them out into a new order

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: An electronic aid to identify an insect, perhaps from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to resolve' rearranges HELP into LEPH.
explanation.definitionFit: African is one of the two main species of this large tusked mammal, the other being Asian.

clue.text: Gives swimmer greeting

parts.note: hands means gives, as in hands over
a hake is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone offers a swimmer a greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimmer' is a crossword favourite for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A handshake is a customary greeting when people meet.

clue.text: Graduate in charge brings in 25 grand

indicators.note: brings in means the degree and charge letters enclose the joke

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
the answer to 25 across is a witty remark, synonymous with jest

explanation.surface: A graduate in charge brings in a quarter of a hundred thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: '25' refers to clue 25 across, a crack or joke, so JEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means impressively grand or stately.

clue.text: Sports equipment bowled unduly leftwards in lapse

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the word for a lapse

parts.note: a fall is a lapse, as a fall from grace

indicators.note: leftwards in an across entry means read from right to left

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
too means unduly, as in too much

explanation.surface: A cricketer's equipment complaint: bowled with an unduly left-leaning action in a lapse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leftwards' turns the bowled-and-unduly string round, and 'in' sets that inside the lapse; 'unduly' is the crossword sense of too, excessively.
explanation.definitionFit: A football is the ball itself, a piece of sports equipment.

clue.text: Boy going round yard snooping

indicators.note: going round means the word for boy turns about

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy circles the yard, prying into things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the boy backwards before the yard abbreviation is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Being nosy is prying into others' affairs, which is snooping.

clue.text: Gunk from mishandled glue's covering daughter

indicators.note: covering means the shuffled letters wrap round the daughter's letter
mishandled means the letters are botched into a new order

explanation.surface: Messy gunk from glue spilt over a daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mishandled' rearranges GLUES as SLUGE, and 'covering' puts D inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sludge is thick, mucky residue, the same as gunk.

clue.text: Country of pronounced beauty and calm

indicators.note: pronounced means the entry is the sound of the words said out loud

parts.note: a belle is a beauty and ease is calm; said together they sound like the country

explanation.surface: A country renowned for its marked beauty and tranquillity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' looks like 'marked' but signals sound: BELLE plus EASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Belize is a Central American nation on the Caribbean coast.

clue.text: Enter president's home moved to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry, north is the top, so this piece goes up to the start

parts.note: Putin is the Russian president
in means at home

explanation.surface: An instruction to go in: the president's residence has been relocated northward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved to the north' shifts IN from the end of PUTIN to the top of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Input, as a verb, means to enter data into a computer.

clue.text: Smooth tongue of Parisian backfiring

parts.note: Polish is a tongue, the language of Poland

indicators.note: backfiring means the French word turns round

parts.note: de is French for of, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A smooth Parisian talker whose words go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backfiring' turns DE into ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Polished means refined and smooth, of a surface or a manner.

clue.text: Female animal, ravenous, emptied containers

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

indicators.note: emptied means the word ravenous loses all its inner letters

explanation.surface: A hungry female animal has emptied the containers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ewers are large water jugs, a kind of container.

clue.text: Crack gadgeteer well-versed about foremost of instruments

parts.note: Q is the gadget-maker in the James Bond films

indicators.note: about means the expert's word wraps round the letter

parts.note: to be up on a subject is to be well-versed in it

indicators.note: foremost of means only the leading letter of instruments is used

explanation.surface: A gadget-maker well-versed in instruments makes a quip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the I of instruments inside UP.
explanation.definitionFit: A crack is a witty remark, and so is a quip.

clue.text: Hold off undoing treat, reward Romeo's left

indicators.note: undoing means the letters are unpicked and reassembled in a new order

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone holds off undoing a treat because the reward's sweetheart left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoing' shuffles TREAT REWARD once one R has left ('Romeo's left').
explanation.definitionFit: To tread water is to mark time and make no move, so to hold off acting.

clue.text: Allow one day to gather one hundred plants

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: to gather means the day's abbreviation collects the numeral inside it

parts.note: Tues is the short form of Tuesday
C is the Roman numeral for one hundred

explanation.surface: Allow one day to harvest a hundred plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to gather' places C inside TUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuces are leafy salad plants.

clue.text: Really, it is always thus

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
so means thus, in that way

explanation.surface: An emphatic remark: really, things are always this way.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal intensifier meaning very or really, as in 'ever so kind'.
